context.description: exception (the context at the exception, like .ecxr) or thread (the context when the dump was written).

symbol.description: module!function+0xoffset, or module+0xoffset when the function has no name.

symbolSource.description: user, pdb, il2cpp, discovered, export, nearest_export (a guess) or none.

kind.description: native, managed (JIT or ReadyToRun code), unloaded_module or unknown.

method.description: How the frame was found: context, unwind_info, epilog, leaf, machine_frame, frame_data (PDB), frame_pointer, call_target (x86: the return address whose call targets this function), scan (heuristic), or clr (the runtime's own stack walk).

basis.description: derived (frame pointer chain, x86 call target) or inferred (a stack scan or a frame chained from one, may be stale; or a nearest-export name); absent when unwind data or the runtime observed it.

token.description: Managed frames: the method token, for decompile_member with assembly.

ilOffset.description: Managed frames: IL offset of the instruction, when the dump holds the JIT's IL map.

assembly.description: Managed frames: id of the loaded assembly that is this build (file name and MVID).

buildCheck.description: Managed frames: match, mismatch (the loaded assembly of that name is another build), or unknown.

statement.description: Managed frames: the C# statement at the IL offset (decompiled with sequence points), for a matching build.

stop.description: Why the walk ended: end_of_stack, max_frames, stack_not_captured, no_unwind_data, left_the_stack, ...

scannedFrames.description: Frames found by scanning the stack, or chained from a frame pointer a scan guessed (basis inferred).

managed.description: Managed frames: decoded (through the runtime's DAC), off, or the DAC status that kept them identified only (not_found, bitness_mismatch, ...); null without a managed runtime.

notes.description: Where the names and unwind data of each module came from, and what was not covered.
